steps.message:
FILES: rich/highlighter.py:101
ROOT CAUSE: The `url` regex in `ReprHighlighter` does not include the `@` character, which prevents URLs containing userinfo (e.g., `https://user@example.com`) from being highlighted correctly.
CHANGE: Update the `url` regex pattern in `rich/highlighter.py` from `r"(?P<url>(file|https|http|ws|wss)://[-0-9a-zA-Z$_+!`(),.?/;:&=%#~]*)"` to `r"(?P<url>(file|https|http|ws|wss)://[-0-9a-zA-Z$_+!`(),.?/;:&=%#~@]*)"` by adding `@` to the character class.
TEST: tests/test_highlighter.py

I have updated the `url` regex pattern in `rich/highlighter.py` to include the `@` character, which ensures that URLs containing user information (e.g., `https://user@example.com`) are highlighted correctly.

Changed file: `rich/highlighter.py` (updated `ReprHighlighter`'s `url` regex).
Test to run: `pytest tests/test_highlighter.py`

arguments.command:
cat > /tmp/repro.py <<'EOF'
from rich.highlighter import ReprHighlighter
from rich.text import Text

highlighter = ReprHighlighter()
url = "https://user@example.com"
text = Text(url)
highlighter.highlight(text)

# The url should be highlighted. 
# In ReprHighlighter, urls are typically highlighted with a specific style.
# We check if the text has any spans applied.
assert len(text.spans) > 0, f"URL {url} was not highlighted"
assert text.spans[0].start == 0
assert text.spans[0].end == len(url)
EOF
python3 /tmp/repro.py; echo EXIT=$?

steps.message: The bug where `@` broke highlighting in hyperlinks has been fixed by updating the `url` regex in `rich/highlighter.py` to include the `@` character. The fix was verified by running the existing test suite and a reproduction script.
